findings.title: Autofocus row shows an editable 'method' chip that the executor ignores, next to a panel saying the real method is something else
findings.what_happened: An Autofocus node's tree row renders 'Autofocus | [vCurve v] | uses defaults'. The Properties panel for the same node, visible at the same time, shows 'Use Settings Defaults [ON] - Using global AF settings' and then 'Global settings: Method = Star HFR, Curve Fitting = Hyperbolic'. I opened the row chip and changed it to 'quadratic'; the row became 'quadratic | uses defaults' and the panel still said Star HFR / Hyperbolic. The chosen value was persisted to the DB (properties {"method":"quadratic",...,"useSettingsDefaults":true}) but per capture_and_guiding.dart:371-374 and autofocus_controls.dart:87-96 it is discarded at run time whenever useSettingsDefaults is true, which is the default.
findings.expected: When 'Use Settings Defaults' is on, the row should show the method that will actually run (Star HFR) or show nothing, and the chip should be disabled. An editable control that has no effect and displays a value contradicted by the panel beside it is a false statement about what the run will do.
findings.repro: Sequencer > Builder > palette search 'autofocus' > click + . Select the node. Read the tree row chip vs the Properties panel 'Global settings' block. Click the row chip and pick 'quadratic'; re-read both.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-16c-afrow.png (row: 'quadratic  uses defaults'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-16b-afpanel.png (panel: Method Star HFR, Curve Fitting Hyperbolic), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-15-afmethod.png (dropdown open, options vCurve/hyperbolic/quadratic)
findings.proposed_fix: In node_summary.dart, when useSettingsDefaults is true emit a StaticFragment showing the effective global method rather than an EditableFragment bound to node.method; only render the editable chip when the node is in 'custom' mode. Also relabel: the node's enum values (vCurve/hyperbolic/quadratic) are curve-fit choices, while the global setting distinguishes Method (Star HFR) from Curve Fitting (Hyperbolic) - the node model conflates two different settings under one name.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced live on display :84, profile sequencer-build-verify. Added an Autofocus node: the tree row renders 'Autofocus | [vCurve v] uses defaults' while the Properties panel on the same screen shows 'Use Settings Defaults [ON] - Using global AF settings' and 'Global settings (edit in Settings > Autofocus): Method = Star HFR, Curve Fitting = Hyperbolic' (/tmp/ns-audit/shots/sbv-07-afadded.png). The chip is a live dropdown offering vCurve/hyperbolic/quadratic (sbv-08-afdrop.png); selecting 'quadratic' changed the row to 'quadratic uses defaults' while the panel still read Star HFR / Hyperbolic (sbv-09-afquad.png). Code confirms the consequence: node_summary.dart:290-297 emits EditableFragment(InlineEditKind.autofocusMethod, method.name) unconditionally, and the executor discards it - serialization_operations.dart:405-417 passes nodeOverrides: n.useSettingsDefaults ? null : n, with useSettingsDefaults defaulting to true (capture_and_guiding.dart:402); device_service/autofocus_controls.dart:96-107 then overwrites effectiveMethod from appSettings.afMethod. Severity corrected P1->P2: the statement is false and the control is dead, but the truthful value is displayed inches away in the same view and an AF-method mismatch does not lose a run's data.

findings.title: Target header card under-reports planned exposures and integration time by the loop multiplier - including for every sequence the app's own Quick-Start Wizard builds
findings.what_happened: I ran the Quick-Start Wizard end to end (M31, 120s, count 10). It produced a Capture Loop with repeatCount 10 containing a single 'Light 1 x 120s' exposure node, all under the M31 TargetHeader. The toolbar reported '10 frames' and the DB stored estimated_duration_mins = 20 (correct). The M31 target header card on the same screen reported 'Ready / 1 planned exposures - 2m'. Ten-fold understatement of both the frame count and the integration time, on the card the user reads to decide whether the night's plan is right.
findings.expected: '10 planned exposures - 20m', matching the toolbar frame count and the stored estimate.
findings.repro: Sequencer > Templates > Quick-Start Wizard. Step 1: RA 0.712, Dec 41.27, name M31. Next through steps 2-5 with defaults. Create Sequence. Read the M31 target card status line, then scroll down to see 'Capture Loop x10 > Light 1 x 120s', then read the toolbar frame counter.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-52-qsbuilt.png ('1 planned exposures - 2m' + toolbar '10 frames'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-54-qstree2.png (Capture Loop x10 containing Light 1x120s), sqlite dump of sequence_nodes for sequence_id=3 showing Loop {"conditionType":"count","repeatCount":10} as the parent of the TakeExposure {"count":1}
findings.proposed_fix: Give visit() a multiplier argument and multiply by LoopNode.repeatCount for count-type loops, exactly as Sequence._countExposures does at sequence_state.dart:168-188. Better: delete _calculateTargetPlan and reuse the model's counting so the two can never diverge again.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced end to end. Ran the Quick-Start Wizard (RA 0.712, Dec 41.27, name M31, 120s, defaults through steps 2-5) and pressed Create Sequence. The built tree is 'Capture Loop x10' containing 'Light 1 x 120s' (sbv-52-tree2.png); the toolbar frame counter reads '10 frames' and the M31 target header card on the same screen reads 'Ready / 1 planned exposures - 2m' (sbv-50-m31seq.png). Saving it stored estimated_duration_mins = 20 for that sequence (sqlite3 /tmp/ns-audit/sequencer-build-verify/data/skotiq.db 'select id,name,estimated_duration_mins from sequences' -> 2|M31 Sequence|20). So toolbar and DB agree at 10 frames / 20m and only the target card is 10x low. Code matches the named location: target_header_card.dart _calculateTargetPlan's visit() (~lines 675-706) recurses into childIds with no loop multiplier, unlike Sequence._countExposures (sequence_state.dart:168-188) which multiplies by LoopNode.repeatCount for count-type loops. Severity corrected P1->P2: it is a false plan summary but display-only, and the correct figure is shown in the toolbar beside it.

findings.title: Sequence Library card reports 10m for a 20-frame sequence - Smart Exposure integration is dropped from the stored duration
findings.what_happened: Built a sequence containing one Take Exposures (10 x 60s) and one Smart Exposure (L, 10 x 60s). The Builder header estimated '~39m 45s' and the toolbar counted '20 frames'. Saving it to the library produced a card reading '2 exposures - 10m', and sequences.estimated_duration_mins in the DB is 10. Bare integration alone is 20 x 60s = 20 minutes. The stored figure equals exactly the ExposureNode contribution (600s); the SmartExposureNode contributes nothing.
findings.expected: The card duration should reflect all imaging nodes. 20 min integration (or the ~40 min run estimate the Builder shows) - anything but half.
findings.repro: Sequencer > Builder > add 'Take Exposures' and 'Smart Exposure' from the palette. Note the Builder header estimate and the toolbar frame count. Sequences tab > Save Current > name it > Save. Read the new card's duration chip, then: sqlite3 /tmp/ns-audit/<profile>/data/skotiq.db 'select name,estimated_duration_mins from sequences;'
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-33-saved.png (card 'M31 | 12 nodes | 1 targets | 2 exposures | 10m'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-07-search-dither.png (Builder header '~39m 30s', toolbar '20 frames'), DB: sequences row 1 estimated_duration_mins=10
findings.where: packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/models/sequence/sequence_models/sequence_state.dart:315-322 (_estimateNodeIntegration handles ExposureNode only); persisted via packages/skotiq_core/lib/src/services/sequence_repository.dart:208 and :239
findings.proposed_fix: Add a SmartExposureNode branch to _estimateNodeIntegration using node.totalIntegrationSecs (already defined at smart_exposure_node.dart:84), mirroring what Sequence.totalExposures already does for the frame count. Note the same stored value feeds LongEstimatedDurationRule (settings_rules.dart:158) and the disk-space rule, so both are currently under-estimating.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced with the exact stated setup. Built a sequence containing Take Exposures (10 x 60s) and Smart Exposure (L, 10 x 60s); the toolbar read '20 frames' (sbv-13-built.png). Saved via Sequences > Save Current; the card reads '5 nodes | 0 targets | 2 exposures | 10m' (sbv-16-saved.png) and the DB row is 1|New Sequence|10. Bare integration is 20 x 60s = 20 min, so the stored value is exactly the ExposureNode contribution (600s) and SmartExposureNode contributes nothing. Code confirms: sequence_state.dart _estimateNodeIntegration (starting line 302) has an ExposureNode branch only and no SmartExposureNode branch, while SmartExposureNode (advanced_nodes/smart_exposure_node.dart:84) does expose totalIntegrationSecs; sequence_repository.dart:208/:239 persist (sequence.totalIntegrationSecs / 60).ceil(). One sub-claim is wrong: the finding says the same stored value also feeds the disk-space rule - disk_space_rules.dart contains no reference to estimatedDurationMins/totalIntegrationSecs. LongEstimatedDurationRule (settings_rules.dart:157) does read sequence.estimatedDurationMins, as claimed. Severity corrected P1->P2 (display/estimate only, no run impact). Note the file path in 'where' is right but the exact line range 315-322 is approximate.

findings.title: Every keyboard shortcut the sequencer advertises is dead in the ordinary state - including the Ctrl+Z that two delete dialogs say is the only recovery
findings.what_happened: The sequencer's own Keyboard Shortcuts sheet (5th tab) lists Alt+1..4, Ctrl+T, Ctrl+Z, Ctrl+Y, Ctrl+D, Ctrl+C, Ctrl+V, Delete, Esc. With an Autofocus node selected (Properties panel showing it) I pressed Delete: nothing. Ctrl+D: nothing. Ctrl+Z after a confirmed node deletion: nothing (the deleted node stayed gone; the toolbar Undo button restored it immediately after). Alt+2, Alt+3 and Ctrl+T never switched tab, even after clicking directly on the tree canvas. The bindings only fired after I clicked a tab-bar button, which happens to move focus into the subtree - Ctrl+D then duplicated correctly (10 -> 11 steps). The delete confirmation dialog states 'This cannot be undone except via Undo (Ctrl+Z)', which is false in exactly the state a user reaches it from (they just typed in the palette search to find the node they are now deleting - that TextField keeps focus and swallows the keys).
findings.expected: Shortcuts listed in the help sheet work whenever the Sequencer screen is showing, regardless of which widget last received a click; and the delete dialog's recovery instruction must be accurate.
findings.repro: Sequencer > Builder > palette search 'delay' > add > click any node row to select it (Properties panel updates) > press Delete, Ctrl+D, Ctrl+Z: nothing happens. Now click 'Sequences' then 'Builder' in the tab bar, click a node, press Ctrl+D: it duplicates. Then press Alt+3 at any time: the tab does not change.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-13-selstate.png (Autofocus selected, Delete/Ctrl+D/Ctrl+Z all no-op), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-94-tab5.png (the shortcuts sheet), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-95-alt3.png (still on Builder after Alt+3 with a node selected), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-10-delete.png (the 'cannot be undone except via Undo (Ctrl+Z)' claim)
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap the CallbackShortcuts subtree in a FocusScope with autofocus, or move the bindings to a Shortcuts/Actions pair registered on the route so they do not depend on a descendant holding primary focus. Make the tree rows themselves focusable so clicking one moves focus into the scope. Until Ctrl+Z is reliable, change the delete-dialog copy to point at the toolbar Undo button, which does work.
findings.verdict_reasoning: The mechanism reproduces, but the title overstates the scope. Confirmed: after clicking the palette 'Search nodes...' TextField and then clicking a node row to select it (Properties panel updates), Ctrl+D and Delete are both no-ops (node count stayed 2 nodes / 1 step), and Alt+3 does not switch tab. Clicking the empty tree canvas afterwards does NOT restore them - Alt+3 still dead (tree still shows 'Tab 1 of 3' toolbox, no Sequence Library). Confirmed the recovery path: after clicking a tab-bar button (Sequences then Builder), Alt+3 did switch to Sequence Library. Confirmed the sheet contents: the 5th tab renders 'Keyboard Shortcuts' listing Alt+1..4, Ctrl+T/Z/Y/D/C/V, Delete, Esc (sbv-56-shortcuts.png). Confirmed the false copy: 'This cannot be undone except via Undo (Ctrl+Z).' appears at delete_node_confirmation.dart:70-75 and batch_operations_toolbar.dart:221-223. REFUTED sub-claim: the shortcuts are not dead 'in the ordinary state' generally - they work whenever focus is inside the CallbackShortcuts subtree (fresh entry / after any tab-bar click); they die specifically once the palette search TextField (or another out-of-scope focusable) takes primary focus. Severity corrected P1->P2: keyboard-only regression with a working toolbar Undo, plus one inaccurate dialog sentence.

findings.title: Snippet palette inserts nothing on tap or on its + button; only drag works, while the panel says 'or tap to insert'
findings.what_happened: The Snippets panel advertises '19 snippets available' and its footer reads 'Drag templates to the sequence tree or tap to insert'. With the root 'Sequence' InstructionSet selected (Properties confirmed: InstructionSet, 3 children) I tapped 'Autofocus Routine' and 'HFR-Triggered AF', and separately clicked each card's explicit '+' button. Node count stayed at 26 and the root stayed at '3 steps' every time. No snackbar, no dialog, and the app log stayed silent. Dragging the same card into the tree with a real press-move-release DID insert it (26 -> 27 nodes, root 3 -> 4 steps).
findings.expected: Tapping a snippet card, or clicking its + button, inserts the snippet - or, if insertion is impossible, says why.
findings.repro: Sequencer > Builder > Snippets tab. Click the root 'Sequence' row in the tree so a container is selected. Tap the 'Autofocus Routine' card body; check the node count in the header. Then click that card's '+'; check again. Then press and drag the card onto the tree and release: only this last one works.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-71-sniptap.png (root container selected, card tapped, header still '26 nodes', root still '3 steps'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-69-snipplus.png (after clicking '+', unchanged), post-drag tree read: '27 nodes' / '4 steps'
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/sequencer/sequencer_screen_parts/snippet_palette.dart:10-33 (onSnippetTap -> withSequenceMutation -> insertSnippet); card affordances in widgets/snippet_palette/actions.dart
findings.proposed_fix: Trace why the tap path never reaches insertSnippet (the drag path shares the same TemplateSnippet payload and works, so the snippet data is fine). Wire the card's + button to the same handler as the drag target, and if withSequenceMutation swallows an exception, surface it - a silent catch on a user-initiated action is what makes this invisible.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced with the root 'Sequence' InstructionSet selected (Properties: InstructionSet, 2 children). Single tap on the 'Autofocus Routine' card body: node count unchanged (2 nodes / 1 step). Click on the card's '+' affordance: unchanged. Footer text confirmed verbatim: 'Drag templates to the sequence tree or tap to insert' (rendering.dart:276; screenshot sbv-10-snippets.png). REFUTED sub-claim: 'only drag works'. A double-click on the same card DID insert (xdotool click --repeat 2 at the same point: 2 nodes/1 step -> 3 nodes/2 steps). Root cause found and it is not a swallowed exception: draggable_item.dart:187-188 binds only onDoubleTap on the desktop path (_buildDesktopItem), and the LucideIcons.plus at :278 is a bare Icon rendered on hover, not a button; the single-tap InkWell exists only on the mobile path (:52-53). So the 'trace why the tap path never reaches insertSnippet' fix note is misdirected, and the 'card affordances in widgets/snippet_palette/actions.dart' pointer is wrong (actions.dart is the overflow menu). Severity corrected P1->P3: two working insert paths exist (double-click, drag) and the Nodes palette footer already says 'double-click to add'; this is a copy/affordance mismatch.

findings.title: Palette search never ranks the exact node-name match first, so typing a node's name adds a different node
findings.what_happened: The palette matches on name OR description and returns results in catalogue order, so a description hit outranks an exact name hit. Three separate searches during this sweep added the wrong node: typing 'Dither' listed 'Smart Exposure' first (its description reads 'handles rotation + dither') and I added a Smart Exposure instead of a Dither; typing 'start guiding' listed 'Photometry Run (template)' first (description 'Center, start guiding, then run AAVSO-grade photometry') and added a 3-child container; typing 'loop' listed 'Instruction Set' first (description 'Group instructions sequentially (no loop)') and added an InstructionSet.
findings.expected: An exact or prefix match on the node NAME ranks above any description match. Typing 'Dither' and clicking the first result must add a Dither node.
findings.repro: Sequencer > Builder > Nodes tab. Type 'Dither' in 'Search nodes...' - Smart Exposure is listed first. Type 'start guiding' - Photometry Run (template) is first. Type 'loop' - Instruction Set is first.
findings.proposed_fix: Score matches: exact name == 100, name startsWith == 80, name contains == 60, description contains == 20; sort descending and keep category grouping only as a visual header. Optionally bold the matched substring so the user can see why a row matched.
findings.verdict_reasoning: All three stated searches reproduce live. 'Dither' -> Imaging category lists 'Smart Exposure' (description 'One row per filter; handles rotation + dither') above 'Dither'. 'loop' -> Logic category lists 'Instruction Set' (description 'Group instructions sequentially (no loop)') above 'Loop'. 'start guiding' -> Science category's 'Photometry Run (template)' (description 'Center, start guiding, then run AAVSO-grade photometry') above Guiding category's 'Start Guiding'. Code matches: sequencer_screen_parts/node_palette.dart:35-50 filters on name.contains(q) || description.contains(q) and preserves catalogue/category order with no scoring; category order in providers/sequence/node_palette.dart is Target, Imaging, Science, Guiding, ... , Logic. Severity corrected P1->P3: every row displays its own name under a visible category header, so this misranks results rather than performing a wrong action; the wrong-node adds in the original sweep were the agent clicking the first row without reading it.

findings.title: Exposure Triggers dialog lets you add and Save a trigger, then silently discards it when the selected node cannot hold triggers
findings.what_happened: With the root 'Sequence' InstructionSet selected I clicked the toolbar bell (Exposure Triggers). The dialog opened, 'Add Trigger' created 'Guiding RMS > 2.0" -> Pause & Recalibrate', and Save closed the dialog with no error. Reopening the dialog showed 'No triggers configured'. Repeating the identical steps with a Take Exposures node selected persisted the trigger correctly. The button is enabled regardless of selection and the dialog gives no indication which node it is editing.
findings.expected: Either disable the toolbar button (with a tooltip: 'select an exposure node') when the selection cannot hold triggers, or tell the user on Save that nothing was stored. Silently accepting and dropping a safety trigger is the worst of the three options - a user who set 'abort if guiding RMS > 2"' would believe they are protected.
findings.repro: Sequencer > Builder > click the root 'Sequence' row > toolbar bell icon > Add Trigger > Save > click the bell again: 'No triggers configured'. Now add a Take Exposures node, select it, and repeat: the trigger is there on reopen.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-74-addtrigger.png (trigger created), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-76-trigreopen.png ('No triggers configured' after Save+reopen, root selected), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-78-trig2.png (same steps with an exposure node selected: trigger persists)
findings.proposed_fix: Resolve the target exposure node up front; if none, disable the toolbar action and put the reason in the tooltip. Show the owning node's name in the dialog subtitle so the user knows what they are editing.
findings.verdict_reasoning: The user-visible defect is real but the stated cause is wrong. REFUTED as written: with the root 'Sequence' InstructionSet selected in a sequence that contained a Take Exposures node, I added 'Guiding RMS > 2.0" -> Pause & Recalibrate', pressed Save, and on reopening the dialog the trigger was still there (sbv-27-trigreopen.png). Selection is irrelevant. CONFIRMED under the real condition: on a sequence with NO ExposureNode (fresh New Sequence, 1 node / 0 steps) the identical steps - Add Trigger (sbv-31-trigadd2.png), Save, reopen - show 'No triggers configured' (sbv-33-trigreopen2.png) with no error. Code explains both: sequence_toolbar.dart:166-195 openExposureTriggers writes the result into every ExposureNode in the sequence via `for (final node in current.nodes.values.whereType<ExposureNode>())`, and currentExposureTriggers() (:156-164) reads from the first ExposureNode; with zero exposure nodes both are no-ops while the success snackbar still fires. The proposed fix (resolve the target exposure node up front, disable with a reason when none) is still the right fix. Severity corrected P1->P2: it only drops the trigger on a sequence that has no exposure node at all, i.e. one that cannot image anything yet.

findings.title: A target named M31 with unset 0,0 coordinates passes validation, and the Slew node confirms in green that it 'Will use target: M31'
findings.what_happened: Added a Target node and typed 'M31' into Target Name. RA/Dec stayed at their 0.0000/0.0000 defaults - there is no name resolution anywhere in the target editor. The tree card then rendered 'M31 / RA 00h 00m 00s Dec +00d 00' 00"'. The Slew node's Properties panel showed a green check and 'Will use target: M31 / 00h 00m 00.0s +00d 00' 00"'. 'Frame target' opened a dialog titled 'Frame target - M31' showing the sky at RA 0.0000h Dec 0.000 deg (Pisces, not Andromeda) with no way to search or fix the coordinates. Pre-Flight Validation raised 9 issues and not one of them was about the coordinates; it only complains when RA is outside 0-24 or Dec outside +/-90 (target_rules.dart:15-35). The DB stored raHours 0.0, decDegrees 0.0 with targetName 'M31'. Running this points the mount at a random patch of sky all night.
findings.expected: Either resolve the name to coordinates (the app clearly can: the bundled 'DSLR M31' starter carries RA 00h 42m 44s Dec +41d 16' 08"), or refuse: a target at exactly 0,0 that the user never typed should be a validation ERROR, and the Slew node must not display a green confirmation for it.
findings.repro: Sequencer > Builder > palette 'Target' > + . In Properties set Target Name = M31, leave RA/Dec. Read the tree card and the 'Frame target' dialog. Add a Slew to Target node and read its Properties. Press Start and read the whole Pre-Flight list.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-21-m31.png (M31 with RA/Dec 0.0000), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-22-frame.png ('Frame target - M31' at RA 0.0000h Dec 0.000), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-23-slew2.png (green 'Will use target: M31 / 00h 00m 00.0s'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-24-preflight.png + 25-pf1/pf2/pf3 (no coordinate issue), DB: TargetHeader properties {"targetName":"M31","raHours":0.0,"decDegrees":0.0}
findings.proposed_fix: Add a TargetCoordinatesUnset rule (error) for raHours==0 && decDegrees==0 with a hint pointing at the resolver. Add name resolution to the Target properties panel using the same targets DAO / catalog path the Quick-Start Wizard uses, and gate the Slew node's green 'Will use target' confirmation on the target actually having coordinates.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced in full. Added a Target node, typed 'M31' into Target Name; RA/Dec stayed 0.0000/0.0000 with no resolver anywhere in the panel, and the tree card rendered 'M31 / RA 00h 00m 00s Dec +00d 00' 00"' (sbv-35-m31.png). Added Slew to Target: its Properties show a green check on a green field reading 'Will use target: M31 / 00h 00m 00.0s +00d 00' 00"' (sbv-37-slew.png). 'Frame target' opened 'Frame target - M31' at RA 0.0000h Dec 0.000 with no search affordance (sbv-44-frame.png). Pre-Flight Validation returned 1 error + 3 warnings - Simulation info, No Exposures, No Mount Connected, No Guider Connected, Guider Not Connected - and nothing about the coordinates (sbv-39/40/41/42). Code confirms: target_rules.dart TargetCoordinatesRule (lines 6-43) only rejects raHours outside [0,24) and decDegrees outside [-90,+90]; grep across providers/sequence/rules found no raHours==0/decDegrees==0 check; target_node_properties.dart (468 lines) contains no resolver/search call. Severity P1 upheld: this is the one finding in the set that can point the mount at the wrong sky for a whole night while the UI affirmatively says the target is set.

findings.title: 'Collapse all' paints a solid grey block over the rest of the sequence tree
findings.what_happened: Clicking the header's 'Collapse' toggle on a 28-node sequence collapses the first two rows correctly and then replaces everything below with one opaque light-grey rectangle filling the remaining tree viewport. The header still reports '28 nodes' and the root still reports '5 steps', so only rendering is broken. It persists across re-screenshots 5s and 20s later. Clicking 'Expand' restores normal rendering; collapsing again reproduces it.
findings.expected: Collapse-all shows one compact row per top-level node.
findings.repro: Sequencer > Builder with a sequence containing at least one nested container (e.g. a Photometry Run template) > click 'Collapse' in the tree header. Wait 5s and look.
findings.where: packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/sequencer/widgets/sequence_tree/support_widgets.dart (_CollapseAllToggle) and the tree's collapsed-row rendering path
findings.proposed_fix: Likely a collapsed row reporting an unbounded/zero intrinsic height that the list then paints as a bare Container. Reproduce under a debug build with the layout explorer on a sequence containing a nested container plus a LiveStacking node.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced independently. Built a 9-node sequence containing a nested container (Photometry Run template, 3 steps) and clicked the tree header's 'Collapse' toggle: the rows above the container render normally and everything from the collapsed container row down is replaced by one opaque light-grey rectangle filling the remaining tree viewport (sbv-23-collapse.png). Header still reports '9 nodes' and root '5 steps', so state is intact and only painting is wrong; still present 12s later (sbv-24-collapse2.png). Toggle label flips to 'Expand'. Location claim checks out: _CollapseAllToggle exists at sequence_tree/support_widgets.dart:887, wired from sequence_header.dart:232. CAVEAT worth recording: both observations (the original sweep's and mine) are on the same softpipe/Xvfb rasterizer, so a Mesa softpipe artifact has not been ruled out - this needs one look on a real GPU before a fix is designed. Severity P2 upheld.

findings.title: Multi-select highlights three rows but the batch bar and the delete confirmation both say two
findings.what_happened: Clicked 'Change Filter' (becomes the primary selection, shown in Properties), then Ctrl+clicked 'Live Stacking' and 'Center Target'. All three rows render with an identical cyan selection border at full zoom, but the batch toolbar reads '2 selected' and pressing its Delete opens 'Delete 2 node(s)?'. The primary selection is drawn as selected while being excluded from every batch operation, and there is no visual difference between the two states.
findings.expected: Either the primary selection joins the multi-select set (count 3), or it is drawn differently (e.g. outline vs fill) so the count and the highlight agree.
findings.repro: Sequencer > Builder > click a node row > Ctrl+click two more rows > compare the highlighted row count with the '<n> selected' chip, then click Delete and read the dialog title.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-62-multisel3.png ('2 selected', three rows outlined), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-64-rows.png (2x zoom: identical borders), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-65-batchdelconf.png ('Delete 2 node(s)?')
findings.proposed_fix: Make the first Ctrl+click seed the multi-select set with the existing primary selection (the behaviour every file manager has), or give multiSelectedNodeIds a visually distinct row treatment.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced. Clicked one Autofocus row (primary selection, shown in Properties), then Ctrl+clicked two more rows. A raw 1:1 capture shows three rows drawn with an identical cyan selection border (sbv-19-multisel3.png) while the batch bar reads '2 selected' (sbv-20-batchbar.png). I also caught the intermediate state: 2 rows outlined, bar reading '1 selected'. The delete-title claim is confirmed in code: batch_operations_toolbar.dart:210 sets count = selectedIds.length (the multi-select set, excluding the primary) and :229 renders 'Delete $count node(s)?'. So the primary selection is painted identically to the multi-selected rows while being excluded from every batch operation. Severity P2 upheld.

findings.title: Mosaic Wizard invents a camera field of view and plans the whole mosaic from it, while the framing dialog on the same screen correctly refuses to guess
findings.what_happened: With no equipment profile configured, the Mosaic Wizard's Plan summary states 'Panel size: 1.00 deg x 0.67 deg' and derives 'Active panels 9 / Grid 3x3 / Est. time 2.3 h / Total exposures 90' from it. Those degrees are the hardcoded field defaults _panelWidthArcmin = 60.0 / _panelHeightArcmin = 40.0, not anything measured from the user's rig. The 'Frame target' dialog, reachable from the same Builder screen, handles the identical missing data honestly: 'No equipment profile with a focal length - set one in Settings to size the framing box.'
findings.expected: Say the FOV is unknown and require a focal length / sensor size (or an explicit override) before quoting a panel size, panel count and total time as facts.
findings.repro: Sequencer > Builder (no equipment profile) > toolbar grid icon (Plan Mosaic). Read 'Panel size' in the Plan summary. Then select a Target node and click 'Frame target' and read its warning.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-79-mosaic.png ('Panel size: 1.00 deg x 0.67 deg'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-22-frame.png (framing dialog admits it cannot size the box)
findings.proposed_fix: Initialise the panel size from the active equipment profile's focal length + sensor dimensions. When that is unavailable, show 'unknown' with the same wording the framing dialog uses and disable 'Load into Sequencer' / 'Create mosaic project' until it is supplied.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced with no equipment profile configured. The Mosaic Wizard's Plan summary states 'Active panels 9 / Grid 3x3 / Panel size: 1.00 deg x 0.67 deg / Overlap 10% / Est. time (14m/panel x 10 subs): 2.3 h / Total exposures: 90' (sbv-43-mosaic.png). Those degrees are exactly the hardcoded field initialisers _panelWidthArcmin = 60.0 and _panelHeightArcmin = 40.0 at mosaic_wizard_dialog.dart:64-65; initState (:105-129) sets only _centerRa/_centerDec and never reads an equipment profile, focal length or sensor size. The contrast claim also holds: the Frame-target dialog on the same Builder screen says 'Field of view unknown - No equipment profile with a focal length - set one in Settings to size the framing box.' (sbv-44-frame.png). One mitigating fact the finding omits: the panel size IS user-editable in the wizard's Advanced section (callback at :891-898), so this is an invented default presented as fact rather than an unchangeable one. Severity P2 upheld.

findings.title: Quick-Start Wizard's target search silently returns nothing on a fresh install
findings.what_happened: Step 1 says 'Search for a target or enter coordinates manually' with a magnifier-prefixed 'Target Name' field hinting 'e.g., M42, NGC 7000, Orion Nebula'. Typing 'M31' shows a brief spinner and then nothing: no results list, no message, RA/Dec stay empty. Pressing Enter does nothing. The cause is that the scratch profile's `targets` table has 0 rows (catalogs not downloaded yet) and the widget has no empty-results branch.
findings.expected: 'No catalog installed - download catalogs in Settings' (or 'No match for "M31"'), so the user knows whether the feature is broken or the data is missing.
findings.repro: Fresh profile. Sequencer > Templates > Quick-Start Wizard > type 'M31' in Target Name > wait > press Enter. Then: sqlite3 <profile>/data/skotiq.db 'select count(*) from targets;' -> 0
findings.proposed_fix: Add an else branch. Distinguish 'catalog empty' (targets table has 0 rows -> link to catalog download) from 'no match' (non-empty catalog, 0 hits).
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced on the fresh scratch profile. Step 1 reads 'Search for a target or enter coordinates manually' with a magnifier-prefixed Target Name field; typing 'M31' produced no results list, no message, and RA/Dec stayed empty (sbv-46-qssearch.png). sqlite3 .../skotiq.db 'select count(*) from targets;' -> 0. Code confirms the missing branch: _target_step.dart:68 is `if (_searchResults.isNotEmpty)` with no else anywhere in the widget. One detail differs cosmetically: the field showed the label 'Target Name' rather than the quoted hint 'e.g., M42, NGC 7000, Orion Nebula' (the hint presumably shows only when the label is not floated). Severity corrected P2->P3: a missing empty-state message on a first-run-only data gap; the manual RA/Dec path on the same step works and the wizard completes.

findings.title: PolarAlignmentNode cannot be added to a sequence - it is absent from the palette
findings.what_happened: PolarAlignmentNode is a full instruction node (model at instruction_nodes/alignment_and_dome.dart:319 with copyWith/serialization) but there is no palette entry for it in any category. Searching 'polar' in the node palette returns zero results, so a user cannot put polar alignment into an automated startup sequence; the only route is the standalone /polar-alignment screen the toolbar compass icon navigates to.
findings.expected: Either a 'Polar Alignment' entry under Mount, or - if the node is deliberately retired - remove it from the model so a sequence file containing one does not deserialize into an unreachable node.
findings.repro: Sequencer > Builder > Nodes tab > type 'polar' in the search field. Zero results. Scroll the full uncollapsed palette: categories are Target, Imaging, Science, Guiding, Mount, Dome, Flat Panel, Focus, Camera, Logic, Timing, Utilities - none contains it.
findings.proposed_fix: Add the entry to the Mount category next to Meridian Flip.

findings.title: Library cards count exposure NODES and call them 'exposures'; the same card's preview then says 'No exposures'
findings.what_happened: A saved sequence containing 20 planned frames (Take Exposures 10 + Smart Exposure 10) shows the chip '2 exposures'. The wizard-built M31 Sequence, which plans 10 frames, shows '1 exposures'. The number is a count of nodes whose specificType is an exposure type, presented with a word that every astrophotographer reads as 'frames'. Expanding the same card's Preview shows 'M31 / No exposures', so one card contradicts itself. 'n targets' is also not pluralised ('1 targets').
findings.expected: '20 frames' (matching the Builder toolbar's own frame counter), and a preview that agrees with the chip.
findings.repro: Sequencer > Sequences tab. Compare each card's 'n exposures' chip with the Builder toolbar's 'n frames' for the same sequence, then click the chevron to expand the card preview.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-33-saved.png ('2 exposures' vs toolbar '20 frames'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-34-cardpreview.png (preview: 'No exposures'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-104-lib3.png ('1 exposures' for a 10-frame sequence, '1 targets')
findings.proposed_fix: Persist a frame total alongside estimated_duration_mins (Sequence.totalExposures already computes it with loop multipliers) and label the chip 'frames'. Pluralise targets. Make the preview walk the same node set as the chips.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced on two saved sequences. A 20-frame sequence (Take Exposures 10 + Smart Exposure 10) shows the chip '2 exposures' against the Builder toolbar's '20 frames'; the wizard-built M31 Sequence, which plans 10 frames, shows '1 exposures' and '1 targets' (sbv-53-lib2.png). Expanding the first card's preview gives 'No targets - 1 exposure node.' - the same card saying 2 in the chip and 1 in the preview (sbv-17-preview.png). Code confirms both halves: sequences_dao.dart:151-153 computes exposureCount as sequenceNodes.id.count(filter: specificType.isIn(_exposureSpecificTypes)) i.e. a node count, rendered as '${_summary.exposureCount} exposures' at sequence_card.dart:247-250 alongside an unpluralised '${_summary.targetCount} targets'; the preview body (:451-457) and _buildTargetPreviewRow's walk (:477-500) both use whereType<ExposureNode>() only, which is why a SmartExposure-only target renders 'No exposures' (:527). Severity P2 upheld.

findings.title: Preflight lists the same missing guider twice as two separate warnings
findings.what_happened: Pre-Flight Validation on a sequence with a Dither node shows both 'No Guider Connected - This sequence includes guiding or dithering operations that require PHD2' and 'Guider Not Connected - Dither requires a guider (PHD2) but none is connected', each with the identical hint 'Connect to PHD2 in the Guiding panel.' Both count toward the '5 warnings' badge, so the summary overstates how many distinct problems exist.
findings.expected: One issue per real problem.
findings.repro: Sequencer > Builder > add a Dither node with no guider connected > Start > scroll the Pre-Flight list.
findings.proposed_fix: De-duplicate by (category, equipment kind) before the dialog renders, keeping the more specific message.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced. With a Dither node and no guider connected, Pre-Flight Validation shows two consecutive Equipment warnings: 'No Guider Connected - This sequence includes guiding or dithering operations that require PHD2.' and 'Guider Not Connected - Dither requires a guider (PHD2) but none is connected.', both carrying the identical hint 'Connect to PHD2 in the Guiding panel.' (sbv-41-pf3.png). Both count toward the badge: the dialog header read '1 error, 3 warnings' where the three warnings are No Exposures + these two. Severity P3 upheld.

findings.title: Palette search with no matches renders a completely blank panel
findings.what_happened: Typing a term with no matches ('polar') empties the whole palette body - no 'no results' text, no suggestion, just black space under the search field. Nothing tells the user whether the search failed or the node does not exist.
findings.expected: 'No nodes match "polar"' with a clear-search affordance.
findings.repro: Sequencer > Builder > Nodes tab > type 'polar'.
findings.proposed_fix: Add an empty state when filteredCategories is empty.

findings.title: Header node count includes the invisible root container, so an empty sequence reads '1 node' next to '0 steps'
findings.what_happened: A brand-new sequence shows '0 targets | 1 node' in the header while the tree body immediately below shows 'Sequence / 0 steps'. Every subsequent count is off by one the same way (9 steps / 10 nodes, 11 steps / 12 nodes).
findings.expected: The header count should match what the user can see and select - the instruction count, not the instruction count plus the implicit root.
findings.repro: Sequencer > Builder > toolbar 'New Sequence'. Read the header chip and the root row on the same screen.
findings.proposed_fix: Count sequence.nodes.length - 1 (or exclude the rootNodeId explicitly).
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced immediately on arrival at the Sequencer: header chip '0 targets | 1 node' with the tree body directly below showing 'Sequence / 0 steps' (sbv-05-seq.png), and the off-by-one held at every size I built (2 nodes/1 step, 5 nodes/4 steps, 9 nodes/5 steps once nesting was added, 17 nodes for the wizard sequence). Code confirms the named location: sequence_tree/sequence_header.dart:216-218 renders '${sequence.nodes.length} ${sequence.nodes.length == 1 ? 'node' : 'nodes'}' with no root exclusion. Note the count is already correctly pluralised there, contrary to the sibling finding about 'Save as Template'. Severity P3 upheld.

findings.title: Validation badges on the sequence header are not clickable, so the only way to read '1 error' is to press Start
findings.what_happened: A newly created empty sequence immediately displays a red '1' and an amber '1' in the header. Clicking either does nothing (they are plain containers). There is no issues panel in the Builder. The only way to learn what they are is to press Start and read the Pre-Flight dialog - which for the empty case turns out to be 'Empty Sequence' and 'No Exposures', i.e. 'you have not built anything yet', shown as a red error on a screen the user just opened.
findings.expected: Clicking the badge opens the same issue list the Pre-Flight dialog shows. And 'you just created an empty sequence' should be an info/hint, not a red error.
findings.repro: Sequencer > Builder > toolbar 'New Sequence'. Click the red '1' badge: nothing. Press Start to discover what it means.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-04-errbadge.png (clicked, no change), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-102-emptypf.png ('Empty Sequence' error + 'No Exposures' warning)
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap the badges in an InkWell that opens the validation issue list read-only.

findings.title: Live Stacking's explanatory helper text is truncated to one ellipsised line
findings.what_happened: Under 'Broadcast mode' the helper reads 'Broadcast only keeps memory clean; Recor...' and under 'Stack combine method' it reads 'Average is fastest; Median+Rej and Sigma r...'. These sentences exist precisely to help the user choose between the dropdown options, and the half that names the alternative is cut off with no tooltip or expansion.
findings.expected: Wrap to as many lines as needed - the panel scrolls anyway.
findings.repro: Sequencer > Builder > add 'Live Stacking' > read the two helper lines in Properties.
findings.proposed_fix: Remove maxLines/TextOverflow.ellipsis from the helper Text widgets.

findings.title: Mosaic preview shows only 5 of 9 panel numbers for a 3x3 grid and hides the centre panel's number under the drag handle
findings.what_happened: With Grid 3x3 and 'Active panels: 9' in the summary, the sky preview draws panel labels 8, 9, 6, 2, 3 and puts the drag-centre handle over the middle cell. Panels 1, 4, 5 and 7 have no visible number, so the user cannot map a panel in the picture to a panel in the plan or know which one they are toggling off.
findings.expected: Every active panel legible and numbered; the drag handle should not sit on top of a label.
findings.repro: Sequencer > Builder > toolbar grid icon (Plan Mosaic) > leave the 3x3 default > look at the sky preview.
findings.proposed_fix: Draw labels after the overlap fills so they are not overpainted, and offset the centre drag handle (or move the centre label).

findings.title: Toolbar's 13 icon buttons expose no accessible names at all
findings.what_happened: The AT-SPI tree for the Sequencer screen contains exactly one named toolbar control: 'button: Start'. The other thirteen actions (New Sequence, Quick-Start Wizard, Calibrate Flat Exposures, Plan Mosaic, Plan Tonight, Open Sequence, Import from NINA/SGP, Save Sequence, Polar Alignment, Exposure Triggers, Slew to Target, Undo, Redo) appear nowhere in the tree and carry no visible text label, only a Lucide glyph. They are unreachable by a screen reader and undiscoverable without hovering each one.
findings.expected: Each icon button exposes its tooltip text as its semantics label, as the tab bar buttons already do ('button: Builder (Alt+1)').
findings.repro:
Sequencer > Builder, then dump the accessibility tree (tools/ui_audit/drive_linux.py tree --profile

): only 'button: Start' appears from the toolbar row.
findings.evidence: tree output in this session vs /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-03-seq.png (13 unlabeled glyphs between Start and the frame counter)
findings.proposed_fix: Wrap each _ToolbarIconButton in Semantics(button: true, label: action.label) - the label strings already exist and are used for tooltips.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced via the AT-SPI dump. A full tree of the Sequencer screen (87 lines, /tmp/ns-audit/tree-sbv.txt) contains only these named buttons: 'Builder (Alt+1)', 'Templates (Alt+2)', 'Sequences (Alt+3)', 'History (Alt+4)' and the tree's own 'button: Sequence'. None of New Sequence / Quick-Start Wizard / Calibrate Flat Exposures / Plan Mosaic / Plan Tonight / Open Sequence / Import from NINA-SGP / Save Sequence / Polar Alignment / Exposure Triggers / Slew to Target / Undo / Redo appears as a control (the 'Slew to Target' and 'New Sequence' hits in the dump are a palette item and the sequence's own name). Code confirms the cause at the named location: sequence_toolbar/icon_and_status.dart:27-35 wraps a bare GestureDetector+Icon in Tooltip(message:) with no Semantics(button: true, label:), while the label strings already exist (sequence_toolbar.dart:439-521). Minor correction: 'Start' appears in the tree as a panel, not 'button: Start'. Severity P3 upheld.

findings.title: 'Save as Template' accepts an empty sequence and says 'This will save 1 nodes'
findings.what_happened: With a freshly created (empty) sequence, Templates > Save as Template opens with the info line 'This will save 1 nodes from the current sequence.' - ungrammatical, and the '1' is the invisible root container. Nothing prevents saving a template with no instructions in it.
findings.expected: Pluralise, count real instructions, and disable Save Template when there are none (with a reason).
findings.repro: Sequencer > Builder > toolbar 'New Sequence' > Templates tab > 'Save as Template'.
findings.proposed_fix: Reuse the same corrected node count as the header fix, pluralise, and gate the primary action.
findings.verdict_reasoning: Reproduced. On a freshly created empty sequence, Templates > Save as Template opens with the info line 'This will save 1 nodes from the current sequence.' and an enabled 'Save Template' button (sbv-55-savetpl.png). Code confirms: the dialog interpolates widget.sequence.nodes.length with a hardcoded 'nodes' at lines 283-285, and the primary action is gated only on _isSaving (line 317), never on node count. Correction to the 'where' field: the file is packages/skotiq_app/lib/screens/sequencer/tabs/templates_tab_parts/_save_template_dialog.dart, not tabs/template_tab/. Note this shares its root cause (counting sequence.nodes.length including the implicit root) with the 'Header node count includes the invisible root container' finding and should be fixed together; it is not a pure duplicate because the missing empty-sequence gate is independent. Severity P3 upheld.

findings.title: Building the standard night by hand takes ~21 actions before configuring anything, and the empty Builder points at none of the faster paths
findings.what_happened: I built cool -> unpark -> slew -> autofocus -> N lights (dither is built into Take Exposures at ditherEvery:3) -> park -> warm by hand. Each node costs three actions with the palette search (click the field, type, click the row's '+') or a scroll-and-click without it, so seven nodes is ~21 actions - and that is before entering a single temperature, exposure or coordinate. Three of my searches added the wrong node (see the ranking defect). Meanwhile the app already has two much better paths: the Quick-Start Wizard produces the same spine plus Plate Solve & Center, Start/Stop Guiding, a HFR refocus trigger, a Weather Safety recovery, a Park-on-Error recovery and a Meridian Flip in about ten actions; and the Starters tab has six curated, well-described sequences. The empty Builder shows neither - just 'Drop instructions here' and a red error badge.
findings.expected: The empty-state canvas should be the entry point: 'Start from a wizard / Start from a starter / Build manually', the way NINA's template gallery and SGP's sequence wizard do. Also add insert-after-selected keyboard entry, since the palette + button already inserts relative to the selection.
findings.repro: Sequencer > Builder > New Sequence, then build the canonical sequence via the palette and count the interactions; compare with Templates > Quick-Start Wizard.
findings.proposed_fix: Replace the bare 'Drop instructions here' with three primary actions. Keep the drop zone below them.

findings.title: Two different things are called Save, two different things are called Templates, and the tab names collide
findings.what_happened: The toolbar floppy icon is 'Save Sequence' and writes a file via the OS chooser; saving your work into the app lives on a different tab as 'Sequences > Save Current'. Separately, the Builder's left panel has a tab named 'Snippets' whose panel header reads 'Templates' and whose search box reads 'Search templates...', while a top-level tab is also called 'Templates' and holds something different (starters + saved sequence templates). A new user cannot tell which Save persists their work or which Templates they are in.
findings.expected: 'Export sequence file...' for the toolbar action and 'Save' for the library action; and one of the two Templates surfaces renamed (the left panel is snippets - fragments - so its header should say 'Snippets').
findings.repro: Compare the toolbar floppy tooltip with Sequences > Save Current; then compare the Snippets tab's panel header with the Templates top-level tab.
findings.evidence: /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-67-snippets2.png ('Snippets' tab, 'Templates' header, 'Search templates...'), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-40-templates.png (the other Templates), /tmp/ns-audit/shots/sequencer-build-31-library.png ('Save Current')
findings.proposed_fix: Rename as above. Low cost, removes a real confusion.

findings.title: Filter is a free-text field with no binding to the wheel; a typo becomes a 2am run failure
findings.what_happened: Change Filter's Properties offers a plain text box pre-filled with 'L' plus an 'Edit filters...' link. Take Exposures shows 'No filters in profile' in the same style. With no wheel connected there is no dropdown, no validation and no autocomplete, so 'Ha' vs 'H-alpha' vs 'HA' is a silent mismatch discovered mid-run.
findings.expected: Bind to the active equipment profile's filter list (a dropdown), with free text only as an explicit override, and validate the name against the profile at build time rather than at run time. NINA and SGP both bind this to the configured wheel.
findings.repro: Sequencer > Builder > add 'Change Filter' > read Properties > Filter Settings.
findings.proposed_fix: Render a DropdownButton over profile.filterNames when available; keep the text field only when the profile has none, and add a validation warning when the typed name is not in the profile.

findings.title: Loop defaults to 1 iteration and Conditional defaults to 'Always Execute' - both are no-ops out of the box
findings.what_happened: A freshly added Loop node has Condition Type 'Fixed Count' and Repeat Count 1, i.e. it wraps its children and changes nothing. A freshly added Conditional has Condition Type 'Always Execute', i.e. it branches on nothing. Both silently do the harmless thing rather than prompting for the value that gives them a purpose.
findings.expected: Loop should default to a meaningful count (or open with the count field focused and empty so it must be set); Conditional should default to a condition that reads as unconfigured and surface a validation warning until it is set.
findings.repro: Sequencer > Builder > add 'Loop', read Properties. Add 'Conditional', read Properties.
findings.proposed_fix: Add a live-validation info rule 'Loop repeats once - it will have no effect' and 'Conditional always executes - no condition set', so the no-op state is at least visible.

findings.title: Quick-Start Wizard shows both a per-filter Count and a Loop Iterations field and never states the resulting frame total
findings.what_happened: Step 2 presents an inline table (Filter | Exposure | Count | Binning) with Count 10 and, directly under it, 'Loop Settings: Fixed Count / Iterations 10'. It is not stated whether those multiply. Step 5 (Review) lists 'Light 10x 120s (1x1)' and 'Loop: Type 10 iterations' and gives no total frame count and no total time. The built sequence turns out to be Loop x10 containing a 1x120s exposure = 10 frames, so the two 10s are the same number expressed twice.
findings.expected: One count field, and a running total on both step 2 and the review step: '10 frames, 20 min of integration, ~24 min with overhead'. That total is the single number a user needs to decide whether tonight's plan fits the window.
findings.repro: Sequencer > Templates > Quick-Start Wizard > step 2 and step 5.
findings.proposed_fix: Collapse the duplicate count into one control and add a totals line derived from the same estimator the Builder header uses.

findings.title: No move up / move down in the node context menu - reordering is drag-only
findings.what_happened: The right-click menu offers Skip to here, Insert Above, Insert Below, Duplicate, Group into Sequential Container, Group into Parallel Container, Disable, Delete - but no way to move the node one slot. On a 28-node tree that scrolls, moving a node past the viewport edge means a drag with autoscroll, which is the least reliable interaction in the whole builder. Separately, 'Group into Sequential Container' is enabled with a single node selected while 'Group into Parallel Container' is greyed out for the same selection, with no explanation for the asymmetry.
findings.expected: Move Up / Move Down entries (and Alt+Up/Alt+Down), plus consistent enablement between the two Group actions.
findings.repro: Sequencer > Builder > right-click any node row and read the menu.
findings.proposed_fix: Add the two entries backed by the same reorder mutation the drag handler calls.

findings.title: Starters tab says 'copy one into your current sequence' but the action replaces the whole sequence
findings.what_happened: The Starters section is captioned 'Bundled, ready-to-run sample sequences. Tap a card to copy one into your current sequence.' Clicking 'Use this starter' discards the current sequence entirely and loads the starter (correctly prompting 'Discard unsaved changes?' first when the sequence is dirty - see verified_correct). 'Copy into' reads as append/merge.
findings.expected: 'Replace your current sequence with this starter.'
findings.repro: Sequencer > Templates > read the Starters caption, then click 'Use this starter' on any card with a non-empty sequence loaded.
findings.proposed_fix: Reword the caption and the button ('Replace with this starter').

verified_correct: Dirty-state guard on destructive loads. I attacked this from both sides: applying a starter template with a just-saved (clean) sequence replaced it silently, which initially looked like data loss - but making one edit first and then applying a different starter raised 'Discard unsaved changes? "DSLR M31 (Andromeda)..." has unsaved changes. Loading "Lunar Terminator..." will discard them' with Cancel / Discard and load. The same guard fired for toolbar New Sequence ('...Discard them and start a new sequence?') and for the Quick-Start Wizard's Create Sequence. Evidence: sequencer-build-43-starter2.png, 51-qsresult.png, 101-newconfirm.png.

Save/update disambiguation. After loading 'Audit Canonical' from the library and pressing Save Current, the dialog changed from 'Save sequence' to 'Update sequence - Overwrite the original or save an independent copy' with two distinct buttons ('Save as new copy' and 'Update "Audit Canonical"'). I specifically tried to make it silently duplicate and it would not. Evidence: sequencer-build-106-savedlg2.png.

Library round-trip fidelity. I saved a 12-node sequence and read the sqlite rows back directly: parent_node_id, order_index and every property blob survive exactly - CoolCamera {targetTemp:-10, durationMins:10}, Dither {pixels:5, settlePixels:1.5, settleTime:30, settleTimeout:120, pattern:random, gridSize:3}, SmartExposure per-filter plans, Recovery thresholds, MeridianFlip {minutesPastMeridian:5, pauseGuiding, autoCenter, refocusAfter, resumeGuiding, failureAction:pauseAndAlert}, TakeExposure {ditherEvery:3}. Nothing was dropped or re-typed.

Duplicate. The library card's copy button produced 'Audit Canonical (Copy)' with all 12 nodes present in sequence_nodes (verified by group-by count in sqlite), and did not touch the original. Tags are deliberately not carried over.
Tag editor. Added 'narrowband', confirmed sequences.tags_json = ["narrowband"] in the DB, and the tag both rendered on the card and produced a working filter chip row above the list.

Delete confirmation and toolbar Undo. The dialog names the node ('Delete "Delay"?'), the batch version names the count and warns about descendants, and clicking the toolbar Undo arrow really did restore the deleted node (9 steps -> 10 steps, 10 nodes -> 11 nodes). Only the Ctrl+Z path is broken (reported separately).
Node disable. The eye icon greys and strikes through the row and flips 'Enabled' off in Properties. Evidence: sequencer-build-96-disabled.png.

Drag interactions. I drove real press/move/release with xdotool: reordering a node within the tree works, dragging a palette node into the tree works, and dragging a snippet card into the tree works (26 -> 27 nodes). Only the snippet TAP and + paths are dead.

Pre-Flight Validation content. Every issue card is specific and carries an actionable hint ('Connect a camera in the Equipment panel', 'Configure an image save location in Settings -> File Output', 'Add exposure or other instruction nodes to the target'), and the Start Sequence button is correctly disabled while errors exist. I tried to start anyway and could not.

Honest empty/unknown states in three wizards. Flat wizard: 'Target signal 50% - camera range not detected'. Smart Night: 'No observer location set - open Settings -> Location...'. Frame target: 'No equipment profile with a focal length - set one in Settings to size the framing box.' These are the correct behaviour that the Mosaic wizard's fabricated panel FOV violates.

Autofocus properties panel surfaces the effective global settings inline (Method, Curve Fitting, Step Size, Steps Out, Exposure, Exposures/Point, Binning, R2 Threshold, Backlash Comp) instead of making the user go to Settings to find out what 'uses defaults' means. Good pattern - it is what exposed the inline-chip defect.

Insert position respects the selection. I checked this deliberately after being misled by AT-SPI child order (which does NOT match visual order in this tree): selecting Cool Camera and adding a Delay inserted it directly after Cool Camera, not at the end. Verified by screenshot, not by tree order.
coverage_note: Drove the real Linux release bundle on display :84 with profile sequencer-build (fresh scratch profile, onboarding skipped), ~110 screenshots, ~35 sqlite queries against /tmp/ns-audit/sequencer-build/data/skotiq.db. Reached 63 of the 90 sequencer screen units and 35 of the 37 seq-node units. Every node type in the palette was added to a live sequence and its Properties panel read; the two unvisited node types are PolarAlignmentNode (absent from the palette - reported as a defect) and PluginInstructionNode (no plugins installed). I built the canonical sequence by hand, saved it, duplicated it, tagged it, re-loaded it, and diffed what the UI claimed against what sqlite stored - that comparison produced three of the four P1 findings. The 27 unreached units are almost entirely run-time surfaces (live frame panel, forensics, session report, replay, handoff, meridian-flip progress, thumbnail strip, critical-event banner) that need an executing run with connected hardware, plus the mobile/narrow layouts. Two builder-scope units are genuinely blocked by the environment rather than by scope: the NINA/SGP import and the file save/export paths open the native GTK chooser, which under Xvfb+softpipe renders as an opaque black window with no window manager (xdotool reports _NET_ACTIVE_WINDOW unsupported), so I could not complete a file round-trip - that is the one gap I would want a follow-up to close on a real desktop session. Two further caveats on my own method: AT-SPI child order does NOT reflect visual order in the sequence tree, so any ordering claim here was confirmed by screenshot; and the harness has no hover, so tooltip-only affordances (the 13 unlabeled toolbar icons) could only be identified from source. No rebuild was performed.
